rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; each credit line 53 names is reached only through a source the tool refuses or reads as Schedule C. The New York City unincorporated business tax credit belongs to a business owner: a sole proprietor files Schedule C (s1.has_sc, which opens the question), and partnership income is refused federally (scope.k1, "income or a loss from a partnership, an S corporation, an estate or a trust? A paper called Schedule K-1 reports it"). The accumulation distribution credit belongs to a trust beneficiary, whose distribution comes on a Schedule K-1 (Form 1041): refused by the same scope.k1. The part-year resident child and dependent care credit needs a part-year City resident, refused on line 1 (ny_it201.gate.part_year_city, "This tool computes the New York City resident tax for a full-year City resident only"). So on a completed return without Schedule C none of the three credits can apply and $0 is right (IT-201-I p. 15, Line 53, "If No, go to line 54").

rulings.restated: (sa helper "Can someone claim you or your spouse as a dependent for 2025, or are you a dual-status alien? (Answer no if the person who could claim you is not required to file and does not file, or files only to claim a refund of withheld or estimated tax.)" = true or helper "The New York item C question, asked only after a federal No; otherwise no" = true)
rulings.model: Item C asks only "Can you be claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's federal return?" The restatement also sets it Yes when the federal answer is Yes only because your spouse can be claimed, or because you are a dual-status alien, and neither is part of item C.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; the restatement's first branch (sa.dependent Yes) is reached only on a return the federal return refuses: sa.deduction refuses when sa.dependent is Yes ("A return for a filer or spouse who can be claimed as a dependent, or a dual-status alien, is outside this resident nondependent slice"), and dual-status aliens are refused again by the scope screen ("For any part of 2025, were you (or, on a joint return, your spouse) a nonresident alien"); a refused federal return is a refused New York return. On every return the tool completes, item C is the New York question "Can you be claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's federal return? Answer Yes even if the other taxpayer did not claim you", which is item C's own text (IT-201-I p. 5, Item C). The spouse and dual-status cases the reply names cannot reach this line.

rulings.restated: (sa helper "Can someone claim you or your spouse as a dependent for 2025? (Answer no if the person who could claim you is not required to file and does not file, or files only to claim a refund of withheld or estimated tax.)" = true or helper "The New York item C question, asked only after a federal No; otherwise no" = true)
rulings.model: Item C asks only "Can you be claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's federal return?", and the restatement answers Yes whenever the federal question about "you or your spouse" is Yes. On a joint return where only the spouse can be claimed it marks Yes, and the New York text does not say how item C treats a spouse.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: ambiguity; amb.ny.2025.item_c. IT-201-I p. 5, Item C: 'If you can be claimed as a dependent on another taxpayer's federal return, you must mark an X in the Yes box.' The project marks item C Yes on a federal Yes to sa.dependent ('Can someone claim you or your spouse as a dependent'), else asks New York's own question. The reply's case, a joint return where only the spouse can be claimed (possible only where the joint return is filed just to claim a refund), is one New York's text does not settle: item C speaks of 'you', and neither the form nor the instructions say how a joint return treats a spouse who can be claimed. The registered ambiguity covers how item C relates to the federal answer; this spouse facet belongs with it (noted for the owner's list). The earlier round's premise that a federal Yes refuses the federal return no longer holds (the Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents is computed, sa.standard_amount), so this is ruled on the text, not on scope.
